verses.verse:
यदाऽरोहेऽवरोहे च विशिष्ट क्रमयोजना।
उच्चारो लययोगेन सैवालंकार उच्यते।१०३।
verses.text: When, in ascent and descent, a particular arrangement of order [among the notes] is made, and it is sounded joined with laya (tempo), that alone is called alaṅkāra (patterned exercise).

commentary.text: That is, when a particular order is arranged among the notes, and ascent and so on are performed with it based on laya (tempo), it is called alaṅkāra (patterned exercise). But bear in mind that an order formed in two or three notes should be carried through the whole ascent and descent. For example, 'Sa Re Ga' and 'Sa Ga Re': both these note groups are made of only three notes, but if the order of the first is 1, 2, 3, then the order of the second is 1, 3, 2. If we carry the first of these orders through 'Re Ga Ma' instead of 'Sa Re Ga', and then through the other notes, the following alaṅkāra will be formed - Sa Re Ga, Re Ga Ma, Ga Ma Pa, Ma Pa Dha, Pa Dha Ni, Dha Ni Ṡa | Ṡa Ni Dha, Ni Dha Pa, Dha Pa Ma, Pa Ma Ga, Ma Ga Re, Ga Re Sa. And by carrying the second order through the other notes - Sa Ga Re, Re Ma Ga, Ga Pa Ma, Ma Dha Pa, Pa Ni Dha, Dha Ṡa Ni | Ṡa Dha Ni, Ni Pa Dha, Dha Ma Pa, Pa Ga Ma, Ma Re Ga, Ga Sa Re - this alaṅkāra will arise.
In alaṅkāras, besides the particular order, there are other subtle elements too.
